---
title: "🌡️ Sea temperature and catch temperature"
description: >
  fao_sst_products(), fao_area_sst(), download_sst_data() and mean_temperature_catch(): the sea
  surface temperature of the FAO fishing areas, how to use your own SST files, and what you must
  check before using the mean temperature of the catch.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
```

The FAO catch statistics give one value per year for each fishing area, without any detail
within the area. The package therefore gives the sea surface temperature (SST) in the same form:
one row per FAO major marine fishing area and year. It uses it to compare the catch with the
temperature of the sea, through the **mean temperature of the catch** (MTC).

## 🌡️ Sea surface temperature of the FAO areas

`fao_area_sst()` returns the yearly SST of the 19 FAO major marine fishing areas. Every call
says which SST data it uses:

```{r, message = TRUE}
sst27 <- fao_area_sst("27")
head(sst27[, c("area_en", "year", "sst_mean", "sst_p10", "sst_p90", "sst_min_month", "sst_max_month")])
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area` | FAO area codes (e.g. `"27"`) or names as in the FAO data (e.g. `"Atlantic, Northeast"`) | `NULL`: all 19 areas |
| `sst` | The SST data: `"ersst5"` (built in), the name of a product downloaded with `download_sst_data()`, or the path of a NetCDF file or of a folder of NetCDF files | the `sst` setting of `fao_settings()`, `"ersst5"` unless changed |
| `variable` | Name of the SST variable in your NetCDF files | `NULL`: found from its name |
| `data_dir` | Folder where downloaded data and computed tables are kept | `fao_data_dir()` |

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product`, `source` | The SST product and the SST data used |
| `area_code`, `area_en`, `year` | FAO area and year |
| `sst_mean` | Mean SST of the area: the mean of the 12 monthly area means (°C) |
| `sst_p10`, `sst_p90` | Range within the area: 10th and 90th percentiles of the yearly SST of its grid cells, weighted by area |
| `sst_min_month`, `sst_max_month` | Seasonal range: the coldest and warmest monthly area means. In areas on both sides of the equator the seasons of the two hemispheres partly cancel, so this range is narrow there |
| `n_cells` | Number of grid cells in the area |
| `downloaded` | Date the data were downloaded or computed |

### The built-in SST: NOAA ERSST v5

The package comes with one SST product, to keep it small:

| | NOAA ERSST v5 |
|---|---|
| Provider | NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information |
| Grid | 2° x 2° (about 220 km), monthly |
| Years in the package | `r paste(range(suppressMessages(fao_area_sst("27"))$year), collapse = "–")` |
| Observations | In situ only: ships and buoys (ICOADS), Argo floats from 1999 |
| Sea ice | About -1.8 °C under ice |
| Licence | NOAA data: may be used and redistributed for free |
| Cite | Huang et al. (2017), see the references |

ERSST v5 is the smallest of the common SST products and is consistent over the whole period, since
it uses no satellite data. Its 2° grid is coarse for small areas: the Mediterranean and Black Sea
(area 37) has only `r suppressMessages(fao_area_sst("37"))$n_cells[1]` cells.

### Using your own SST data

Any other gridded SST can be used by giving the **path of its NetCDF file, or of a folder of
NetCDF files**, either for one call or once for the session:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_area_sst("27", sst = "D:/data/HadISST_sst.nc")       # one call
fao_settings(sst = "D:/data/HadISST_sst.nc")             # all functions, for the session
mean_temperature_catch(FAO27$area_data)                  # now uses this file
fao_settings(sst = "ersst5")                             # back to the built-in SST
```

The files are read as follows:

- They must hold an SST variable with **longitude, latitude and time**, monthly or daily
  (e.g. HadISST, COBE-SST2, OISST, ERSST, or a climate model output). The variable is found by
  its name (`sst`, `analysed_sst`, `tos`, ...); give it as `variable = "..."` if not.
- Longitudes may run from -180 to 180 or from 0 to 360. Values in kelvin are converted to °C.
  If there are several depths, the first (the surface) is used. Values below -5 °C, which some
  products use to mark sea ice (-1000 in HadISST1), are set to -1.8 °C.
- Daily values are averaged by month, and only years with all 12 months are kept. Grids finer
  than 1° are first averaged to about 1°.
- The yearly area means are computed the first time, which can take a few minutes, and saved in
  the `sst` folder of `fao_data_dir()`. Later calls with the same files read the saved table;
  if the files change, the table is computed again.
- Reading NetCDF files needs the ncdf4 package (Pierce 2025): `install.packages("ncdf4")`.

### Downloading common SST products

`fao_sst_products()` (no arguments) lists the products the package knows, with their provider,
grid, first year, data sources, treatment of sea ice, licence, reference (`citation`, `doi`), web
page (`homepage`), download server and approximate size per year (`mb_per_year`):

```{r}
knitr::kable(fao_sst_products()[, c("product", "name", "grid", "first_year", "data_sources", "mb_per_year")])
```

`download_sst_data()` downloads one of these products, one year at a time, and computes its
table. It is then used by its name, e.g. `sst = "hadisst1"`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
download_sst_data("hadisst1")                 # about 240 MB; run again to resume
fao_area_sst("27", sst = "hadisst1")
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `product` | `"ersst5"`, `"hadisst1"`, `"cobe2"` or `"oisst21"` (for ERSST v5, whose table is built in, the years published since are added) | `"ersst5"` |
| `years` | Years to download | `NULL`: from 1950 (1982 for OISST v2.1) to the last complete year |
| `data_dir` | Folder where the files are kept (in its `sst` folder, with `files.csv` recording where and when each was downloaded) | `fao_data_dir()` |
| `overwrite` | Download again the years already downloaded | `FALSE` |
| `quiet` | Print no progress messages | `FALSE` |

Years already downloaded are skipped, so an interrupted download is resumed by running the
function again. It returns the area table, as `fao_area_sst()`. SST products use different
observations and methods (HadISST1: Rayner et al. 2003; COBE-SST2: Hirahara et al. 2014; OISST
v2.1: Huang et al. 2021), so their values and trends differ somewhat. Repeating an analysis with a
second product shows how much a result depends on the product.

### How the area means are computed

Each grid cell counts for each FAO major area it overlaps, weighted by the area of the overlap
computed on the sphere. Cells on a boundary between two areas are shared, and coastal cells
count for their sea part only. The areas are those of the FAO map in the package (the 19 marine
areas of the CWP handbook). Values over the Arctic Sea and the Antarctic areas partly reflect sea
ice rather than measured water temperature.

### 🧩 Subareas and divisions (extension)

`fao_area_sst(level = "division")` gives the SST of the FAO subareas and divisions, the units of
the catch data by division (`load_fao_divisions()`, see [💾 FAO data](data.html)). The built-in
ERSST v5 table covers the subareas and divisions of areas 34, 37, 47 and 51; downloaded products
and your own NetCDF files give all of them.

```{r, message = TRUE}
div <- fao_area_sst(level = "division")
show_table(subset(div, startsWith(area_code, "37.") & year == 2024)[, c("area_code", "area_en", "sst_mean", "n_cells")], n = 12)
```

Many divisions are small for a 2° grid: the Sea of Marmara and the Sea of Azov have one or two
cells. A finer product, given as the path of its NetCDF files, suits divisions better.

## 🐟 Mean temperature of the catch

The mean temperature of the catch (MTC; Cheung et al. 2013) is the average preferred temperature
of the species caught, weighted by their catch:

$$MTC_t = \frac{\sum_i T_i C_{i,t}}{\sum_i C_{i,t}}$$

where $T_i$ is the preferred temperature of species $i$ and $C_{i,t}$ its catch in year $t$; both
sums are over the items that have a preferred temperature. A rising MTC means that species of
warmer waters make up a larger part of the catch.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
FAO27 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Northeast", plot = FALSE)
mtc <- mean_temperature_catch(FAO27$area_data)
mtc$trend      # slopes (°C per decade), Mann-Kendall test, correlation with SST
```

The preferred temperatures come from FishBase and SeaLifeBase (`TempPrefMean`), matched to the
FAO species items by `fishbase_match()`; how the data are obtained and matched is explained in
[🐠 FishBase and SeaLifeBase traits](fishbase.html). With the default `version = "latest"`, the
first run downloads the FishBase and SeaLifeBase tables it needs (about 23 MB) when online;
offline, it uses the newest downloaded release, or else the table built into the package.
`version = "builtin"` always uses the built-in table, without download.

The chart shows the MTC with the SST of the area (and its range within the area) and, below, the
share of the catch that has a preferred temperature (the coverage). Years in which this share is
below `min_coverage` are faded and left out of the trends. Trends are computed over all years and
over the years from `trend_from`: the slope of a linear regression (°C per decade), a Mann-Kendall
test (Mann 1945; Kendall 1975) corrected for autocorrelation as in `peak_trend()` (Yue and Wang
2004), and the Pearson correlation of MTC and SST,
for the series and for their year-to-year differences.

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `area_data` | FAO catch data: `fishing_area_data()$area_data`, or any subset of `load_fao_data()` (several areas give one MTC per area) | required |
| `version` | FishBase and SeaLifeBase release, e.g. `"26.06"`; `"builtin"` for the table built into the package (see `fishbase_match()`) | `"latest"` |
| `min_coverage` | Minimum share of the catch (%) made up by items with a preferred temperature; years below it are faded, marked in the table and left out of the trends and correlations (`0` keeps all years) | `50` |
| `trend_from` | First year of the second trend period (the period studied by Cheung et al. 2013 starts in 1970) | `1970` |
| `use_match` | Kinds of match (`match_type` of `fishbase_match()`) whose preferred temperature is used | `c("exact", "synonym", "WoRMS valid name (exact)", "WoRMS valid name (synonym)", "manual")` |
| `match` | A checked match table to use instead of running `fishbase_match()`: a data frame, or the path of a CSV file such as the species table of a previous run (needs `species_en`, `match_type` and `temp_pref_mean`) | `NULL` |
| `sst` | SST to compare with: `"ersst5"`, a downloaded product, the path of NetCDF files, `FALSE` for none, or a data frame with `area_code` (or `area_en`), `year` and `sst_mean` (optionally `sst_p10`, `sst_p90`) | the `sst` setting of `fao_settings()`, `"ersst5"` unless changed |
| `plot` | Save the charts in `figures/png/summary/` | `TRUE` |
| `table` | Save the tables in `tables/` | `TRUE` |
| `lang` | Language of the chart text and names: `"en"`, `"zh"` or `"both"` | `NULL`: the language of `fao_settings()` |
| `pptx` | Also save the charts as editable PowerPoint files in `figures/pptx/summary/` | `FALSE` |
| `plot_show` | Also draw each chart in the plot window (e.g. the Plots pane of RStudio) as it is saved | `FALSE`, or `plot_show` of `fao_settings()` |
| `label` | Name at the start of the output file names | the fishing area (or country) of the data |
| `data_dir` | Folder where downloaded data are kept | `fao_data_dir()` |

The function returns `yearly` (MTC, coverage, SST and its product by area and year), `trend`
(slopes, Mann-Kendall tests and correlations by area and period) and `species` (one row per
area and FAO species item).

### 🧩 By division (extension)

With catch data by division, `by = "division"` gives the MTC of each division, compared with the
SST of the division:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
med <- load_fao_divisions("GFCM")
mtc_divisions <- mean_temperature_catch(med, by = "division")
```

Divisions without a boundary on the FAO map use the SST of their subarea (column `sst_unit`),
codes that are not places (e.g. 37.0.0 Tunas) have no SST, and the function says which divisions
have fewer than 5 grid cells.

### ⚠️ What the package does, and what you must check

The package computes the MTC, its trends and its comparison with SST. The preferred temperature
of each species is **not** checked by the package. It is a first, automatic match of the FAO
scientific name to FishBase or SeaLifeBase (`TempPrefMean`), given with the links needed to
check it. Names do not always match between databases (Grenié et al. 2023), so whether each match
and its temperature are right must be judged by you, from these pages and the literature, before
the results are used:

1. Open the species table, `tables/<label>_mtc_species.csv`. Items are sorted by catch, so the
   first rows matter most.
2. For each item used (`used` is TRUE), open `url` (the FishBase or SeaLifeBase page of the
   matched species), `search_url` and `worms_url` (the World Register of Marine Species). Check
   that the matched species is the FAO item, and that its preferred temperature is plausible
   for the stock in the area.
3. Write who checked it, or the date, in the column `checked`. Correct a wrong value in
   `temp_pref_mean` and give its source in `note` (to use a value for an item that is not used,
   such as a genus, also set its `match_type` to `"manual"`); or record the correction in the
   corrections file of `fishbase_match()`, which every later run applies.
4. Run the function again with the checked table:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
mtc <- mean_temperature_catch(FAO27$area_data, match = "tables/Atlantic__Northeast_mtc_species.csv")
```

Until every item used has been checked, the function says how much of the catch has been checked,
and the chart caption says that the preferred temperatures have not all been checked.

### Limitations

- **Preferred temperatures.** FishBase gives `TempPrefMean` as an estimate from AquaMaps maps,
  computed with an unpublished script (Froese 2020), and does not document which map cells and
  which temperature (surface or bottom) it uses. For some species it is far below the temperature
  of the area where most of their catch is taken: it is 10.3 °C for European pilchard, 83% of
  whose catch (2015-2024) is taken in area 34. Cheung et al. (2013) used the median of a
  temperature profile computed from modelled distributions instead, as did most regional
  studies (Tsikliras and Stergiou 2014; Liang et al. 2018), while Dimarchopoulou et al. (2022) and
  Lavin et al. (2023) used the FishBase mean, as here. MTC values of the package are therefore not
  directly comparable with published ones.
- **Coverage.** Items above species level (e.g. "Marine fishes nei") are left out, as in the
  published studies. Their coverage ranges from below 30% to over 90% (Tsikliras et al. 2015;
  Liang et al. 2018), and no published study sets a minimum; `min_coverage = 50` is a convention
  of the package. More catch is reported by species over time, without earlier years being
  revised (Garibaldi 2012), and catches move between areas or are reported as "nei" (FAO 2024),
  which changes the MTC without any change in temperature.
- **Causes.** The MTC also changes with the species fished, fishing grounds, gear, markets,
  management and reporting, not only with temperature (e.g. Alajmi et al. 2024; Lavin et al.
  2023). Check which items drive a change (`weight_pct`, `contribution_c` in the species table)
  before attributing it to warming.
- **Statistics.** Trends are linear slopes and Mann-Kendall tests; the comparison with SST uses
  correlations of the series and of their year-to-year differences. Both series are
  autocorrelated: the Mann-Kendall test is corrected for it (Yue and Wang 2004), but the p-values
  of the slopes and correlations are too small (Yue et al. 2002; Pyper and Peterman 1998), and
  the correlation of differences can miss a relation that acts only over decades. In the Adriatic
  Sea, the relation of MTC with SST was no longer significant once autocorrelation was accounted
  for (Kamberi et al. 2025).

### Files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `figures/png/summary/<label>_mtc.png` | MTC and SST (with its range in the area); for one area, the coverage below |
| `figures/png/summary/<label>_mtc_coverage.png` | Coverage of each area (several areas only) |
| `tables/<label>_mtc.csv` | Yearly MTC, coverage, SST and the SST data used |
| `tables/<label>_mtc_trend.csv` | Slopes, Mann-Kendall tests and correlations with SST |
| `tables/<label>_mtc_species.csv` | Each species item: preferred temperature, catch, weight, contribution, match, links, `checked` and `note` |

## 📝 In the Word report

`fao_report()` adds a section on the mean temperature of the catch with `mtc = TRUE` (see
[📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF](report.html)). The report uses the FishBase data bundled with the
package (`mtc_version = "builtin"`), so it needs no download and gives the same values on every
computer; `mtc_version = "latest"` uses the newest FishBase release instead. The other settings
of `mean_temperature_catch()` are given with the prefix `mtc_`, e.g. `mtc_sst = "hadisst1"` or
`mtc_match = "<checked species table>"`. The species used, with their matches and links, are
returned as `report$mtc_species` for checking:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
report <- fao_report(27, mtc = TRUE, mtc_min_coverage = 60)
report$mtc_species
```
